title: Runtime rollback scenario catalog and SLO impact mapping
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This document is a curated catalog of realistic runtime rollback scenarios for the Redwood serving platform, paired with a deterministic SLO impact mapping and step-by-step operator checklists. It is written for platform operators, oncall engineers, and SREs to improve response consistency, speed, and post-incident learning.

Scope
-----
- Applicable systems: inference runtime (request router, batching layer, KV prefix cache), model variant service, compiler/kernel selector, regional allocator, and prefetch coordinator.
- Not covered: billing reconciliation, legal/compliance notifications, or customer-facing postmortem text (see escalation-playbook).

Why this exists
----------------
- Rollbacks are common and high-risk; ad-hoc decisions increase blast radius.
- Quantifying SLO impact for each rollback path reduces decision inertia.
- Standardized checklists reduce operator cognitive load during high-severity events.

Owners and stakeholders
-----------------------
- Primary owner: Platform SRE (team: eng-platform)
- Runtime product owner: Runtime Team (eng-serving-runtime)
- Oncall escalation: Platform oncall -> Runtime oncall -> Incident Commander
- Communications: Customer Success for enterprise customers, Growth for self-serve anomalies

Document structure
------------------
1) Scenario catalog (narrow, descriptive titles)
2) SLO impact mapping (per-scenario token latency / availability / error profile)
3) Decision matrix (fast path rules for rollback vs. mitigation)
4) Operator checklist & explicit CLI/console commands
5) Verification and observability dashboard panels to consult
6) Post-incident synthesis template and retrospective triggers
7) Simulation & safety lab guidance for periodic drills

1) Scenario catalog (examples)
--------------------------------
Each scenario below includes: trigger conditions, likely root causes, expected immediate effects, recommended containment, rollback path, and estimated SLO impact (quantified where possible).

Scenario A: Kernel regression after compiler push
- Trigger: Sudden tail-latency spike (p99 > 3x baseline) across a single model family immediately after a compiler-subsystem deploy.
- Probable causes: new kernel selection default, missing optimized path for attention kernel, micro-batching mismatch.
- Immediate effects: p95/p99 latency increase, token throughput decrease, CPU/GPU utilization skew, increase in model-in-flight queue depth.
- Recommended containment: Immediately disable new kernel flag (feature-flag toggle) or rollback compiler image to last-known-good.
- Rollback path (fast): Revert compiler image in canary region -> progressive global revert if metrics do not recover in 5 minutes.
- Estimated SLO impact: 10–25% p99 SLO burn during 5–20 minutes depending on traffic profile; availability impact minimal if autoscale compensates.

Scenario B: Model variant introduces hallucination/regression (quality regression)
- Trigger: Quality regression alert from evals (user-reported or automatic prompt-set drift) after model variant rollout.
- Probable causes: model weights mismatch, quantization artifact, prompt template change.
- Immediate effects: downstream customer errors, surge in corrective retries, potential increase in token usage.
- Recommended containment: Pause rollout and route traffic to previous stable variant (runtime model-router TTL-based pin).
- Rollback path (fast): Traffic reroute to pinned stable model variant with immediate canary verification.
- Estimated SLO impact: Minimal latency change; potential cost/SLA impact from increased retries and manual mitigation.

Scenario C: KV prefix cache corruption on a subset of nodes
- Trigger: Elevated error rates for prefix-cache dependent requests, cache-miss ratio abnormal, partial 5xx increases.
- Probable causes: metadata desync during shard rebalance, mismatched schema after a metadata migration.
- Immediate effects: elevated tail latency, increased origin hits, reduced effective throughput.
- Recommended containment: Isolate affected cache shards, enable degraded-read mode (serve from origin with degraded TTL), and mark shards for rehydration.
- Rollback path (fast): Revert metadata migration or rollback rebalancer orchestration job.
- Estimated SLO impact: 5–15% unit cost increase; p95 latency uplift 20–40% for affected cohorts.

Scenario D: Regional allocator mis-allocation leading to cold-start storm
- Trigger: Unusual cross-region traffic shift or autoscaling misconfiguration causing mass cold starts and thermal evictions.
- Probable causes: allocator policy regression, incorrect warmset population, prefetch polling disabled.
- Immediate effects: transient high latencies, token drops, queue growth, and potential thermal throttles on GPU nodes.
- Recommended containment: Enable cross-region traffic steering to healthy region, emergency warmset reinflation, or enable burst credits for high-priority tenants.
- Rollback path (fast): Revert allocator policy commit; roll back last config change to allocation heuristics.
- Estimated SLO impact: Availability risk for large tenants; p99 could be breached for 10–30 minutes depending on refill speed.

Scenario E: Request router regression (header parsing / auth)
- Trigger: Elevated 4xx errors or malformed request errors after router config change.
- Probable causes: new header validation rule, auth token parsing bug, CLI-driven routing rule misapplied.
- Immediate effects: broad request failures, customer-visible 4xx/401s.
- Recommended containment: Disable strict validation rule; add temporary permissive header-compat path.
- Rollback path (fast): Rollback router config via versioned config store and restart router pods with zero-downtime strategy.
- Estimated SLO impact: Immediate availability impact for affected request types; rapid rollback typically restores within 2–10 minutes.

2) SLO impact mapping (summary table / guidance)
- Latency SLOs to consider: p50, p95, p99 token latency per model route; per-tenant availability SLO (requests succeeded / requests attempted); error budget burn rate.
- Mapping guidance (quick reference):
  - If p99 increases by >2x for >5 minutes for a single model family -> escalate to SEV2 and consider rollback.
  - If availability drops >1% for >10 minutes for >1 enterprise tenant -> SEV1 and forced rollback unless remediation is immediate.
  - If cost (tokens or GPU-hours) increases >30% sustained for 15 minutes due to retries or amplification -> consider traffic shaping and rollback of recent changes.

3) Decision matrix (fast-path rules)
- Fast rollback (immediate action) when any of the following are true:
  1) p99 spike >3x and correlated with deploy timestamp within last 10 minutes.
  2) Any config change that causes >5% increase in 4xx/5xx within 5 minutes.
  3) Automatic quality regression detection (evals) detects >10% drop in pass-rate for a monitored prompt-set.
- Hold-and-mitigate (operator-led) when:
  1) Impact is isolated to a small percentage (<2%) of traffic and a graceful degraded mode exists.
  2) Rollback itself carries >5% risk to availability (e.g., schema migrations).
- Manual review required when: rollback requires data migration reversal, non-trivial stateful revert, or customer data concerns.

4) Operator checklists (runnable steps)
- Pre-rollback (0–2 minutes)
  1) Record incident id, oncall names, and snapshot top-5 symptoms in incident doc.
  2) Confirm deploys/config changes in last 30 minutes (gitops commits, CI deploy IDs).
  3) Identify affected routes/tenants (query traces by model id and tenant id).
  4) Take a short-lived traffic-snapshot (5-minute window) to capture metrics.
- Execute rollback (2–10 minutes)\  
  1) If feature-flag: flip flag to previous state and validate health endpoints (curl /health).
  2) If image rollback: trigger canary revert via deploy orchestrator: ci/CD rollback command: 
     - CLI example: rci rollback deploy --service runtime-compiler --image sha-abcdef --region us-west-2
  3) If config rollback: revert config tag in config-store and restart router pods with rolling restart (no drain if risk of capacity blowout).
  4) If model variant: use model-router CLI: model-router promote --variant stable --model M123 --weight 100
- Immediate verification (5–20 minutes)
  1) Validate health: synthetic canary queries for the affected model (10 requests at expected p95 token length).
  2) Observe SLOs: p50/p95/p99, error rate, quota burn, GPU utilization.
  3) If no improvement in 5 minutes, escalate to IC and consider deeper rollback (region-level).

5) Observability panels and alerts to consult
- Minimum dashboard set to view during rollback:
  - Model-family latency heatmap (p50/p95/p99) by region
  - Router error distribution (4xx/5xx) by route and tenant
  - Kernel/Compiler rollout telemetry (canary vs. global)
  - KV prefix-cache metrics: hit ratio, rehydration queue, shard error counts
  - Cost signal: tokens/sec and GPU-hours rolling 1m/5m/15m
- Alert tuning recommendations: enrich alerts with last-deploy metadata, recent config commits, and suspected change-id to reduce investigation time.

6) Communication templates (operator-friendly snippets)
- Short internal update (status channel):
  - "INC-XXXX: Observed p99 x3 for model M123 after compiler canary deploy. Reverted compiler canary at t+3m. Monitoring for recovery; next update in 10m. Owner: @runtime-oncall."
- Customer-facing (enterprise):
  - "We observed elevated inference latencies for model M123 beginning at 12:03 UTC after an internal compiler change. We reverted the change and are monitoring; expected full recovery within 15 minutes. We will follow up with a technical summary."

7) Post-incident synthesis and retrospective triggers
- Immediate postmortem steps (within 24–72 hours):
  1) Capture timeline (deploys, metrics, operator decisions).
  2) Run prereq checks: reproduce in synthetic-lab if safe.
  3) Identify root cause and whether rollback prevented customer impact.
  4) Document actions: engineering fixes, monitoring gaps, and mitigation automations.
- Retrospective triggers (create retro if any of these occurred):
  - SEV1 or >50% error-budget burn for any SLO.
  - Rollback caused cascading degradation in another service.
  - Rollback itself required manual data migration reversal.

8) Simulation & safety lab guidance
- Quarterly simulated rollback drills: run full checklist in a staged environment with realistic traffic replay.
- Safety lab test cases:
  - Canary compiler revert under steady traffic; measure p99 delta and recovery time.
  - Model variant swap with controlled quality-eval guardrails enabled.
  - Cold-start allocator misallocation simulation to validate warmset reinflation procedure.
- Automation opportunities: automate the short-lived traffic snapshot collection and attach to incident doc; build a pre-flight 'rollback risk' signal that estimates SLO-cost of revert.

Appendix A: Useful CLI commands and playbook snippets
- rci list-deploys --service runtime-compiler --since 1h
- rci rollback deploy --service runtime-compiler --image sha-abcdef --region us-west-2
- model-router snapshot --model M123 --variants
- ttlctl mark-degraded --shard sh-17 --reason "rehydrate"

Appendix B: Example dashboard widget specs (text table)
- Widget: Model latency sparkline | Metrics: model.M123.latency.p95 | Window: 5m
- Widget: Error distribution table | Metrics: router.errors{status=4xx,5xx} by route | Window: 10m

Appendix C: Post-rollback verification checklist (operator sign-off)
- [ ] Synthetic canary queries succeed (>= 95% within p95 baseline)
- [ ] No sustained error-rate increase for affected tenants
- [ ] Deploy/config reverted matches last-known-good commit id
- [ ] Incident doc includes timeline, decision rationale, and next steps

Appendix D: Roadmap items (actions to reduce rollback frequency and cost)
- Implement automated rollback-risk estimator (Q2 2026).
- Expand canary synthetic coverage to include quality-eval prompt-sets (Q3 2026).
- Add preflight rollback simulation in CI for compiler and allocator changes (Q4 2025).
- Build 'safe-revert' state machine that checks migration safety and coordinates multi-service rollbacks (Q1 2027).

Contact and feedback
---------------------
- For questions or to request additional scenarios, add a comment on this page or ping @Aisha.Patel in #platform-ops.
